angle_name: Square-hyperbola zero-mode cancellation via signed Λ-dispersion
mechanism: Put D=y and X=(D+1)^2-1. First replace π-Li by the Stieltjes transform of E(N)=ψ(N)-N, retaining the prime-power correction as a separate signed term. For A_D(z)=Σ_{d≤D} μ(d)E(⌊z/d⌋), exact convolution gives A_D(z)=-1-Σ_{n≤z}μ(n)log n-Σ_{m≤D}(Λ(m)-1)(M(⌊z/m⌋)-M(D)) throughout z∈[X-D,X]; the upper limit m≤D is stable because this is the canonical square window. Decompose the last two terms together into dyadic multiplicative packets and prove dispersion for their difference, not separate bounds. The zero-frequency contribution is cancelled algebraically by μ*Λ(n)=-μ(n)log n; nonzero packets are attacked by a hybrid multiplicative large-sieve/TT* estimate over the D endpoint translations. Smooth logarithmic weights are inserted before estimating, and the sparse Λ-θ prime-power layers are treated by the same signed packet estimate. Partial summation then transfers the ψ estimate to the Abel face.
new_leverage: This uses three facts simultaneously that the killed routes did not: the canonical window makes the complementary hyperbola edge exactly stable and symmetric; μ*Λ supplies an exact signed cancellation of the otherwise fatal zero mode; and translation averaging supplies a genuine frequency family for the remaining packets. Thus it exits the F-closure rather than improving a Cauchy-Schwarz bound, uses the amended pinned-to-window bridge, and enters precisely the signed-contraction door left open by obstacle 9.
target_estimate: Signed square-hyperbola dispersion: uniformly for X=(D+1)^2-1, H=D, and the logarithmic weights required by Stieltjes partial summation, prove (1/H)Σ_{0≤t<H}|Σ_{d≤D}μ(d)(ψ(⌊(X-t)/d⌋)-⌊(X-t)/d⌋)|^2≪ε X^{1+ε}, together with the analogous X^{1+ε} bound for the signed prime-power removal term. The exact hyperbola identity reduces the first estimate to an L2 cancellation between -Σ_{n≤X-t}μ(n)log n and Σ_{m≤D}(Λ(m)-1)(M(⌊(X-t)/m⌋)-M(D)).

obstacle_positions.1: Passed structurally: μ and Λ-1 remain coupled until after μ*Λ=-μ log cancels the zero mode; no M^2 input is recombined by absolute inequalities.
obstacle_positions.2: Avoided: TT* is organized by translation frequencies and dyadic product packets, not by a bounded-fiber pair-to-modulus map.
obstacle_positions.3: Used essentially: every estimate is on the specific backward window at X=(D+1)^2-1, where the complementary support m≤D is exactly stable.
obstacle_positions.4: Irrelevant: only packet lengths, additive translation frequencies, and small dyadic conductors occur; no primorial or full-wheel modulus is introduced.
obstacle_positions.5: Not sieve-only: the decisive cancellation is the signed convolution identity involving μ; parity remains a danger only if TT* takes absolute values before that identity is used.
obstacle_positions.6: No pointwise bound for R and no absolute sum over zeros is assumed; a zeros implementation would be rejected unless it reproduces the algebraic zero-mode cancellation and controls off-line terms collectively.
obstacle_positions.7: Finite computations may falsify the proposed packet contraction or locate a bad scale, but favorable data are assigned no evidentiary role.
obstacle_positions.8: Individual floor jumps are never bounded by polylogarithms; the argument allows Wigert spikes and estimates the complete canonical-window L2 norm.
obstacle_positions.9: This explicitly takes the sole surviving route: a signed contraction/cancellation between the log-Möbius full convolution and the two-parameter complementary edge, never an absolute renewal induction.

kill_test: On exact arithmetic data, form the dyadic packets of F_t=-Σ_{n≤X-t}μ(n)log n and B_t=Σ_{m≤D}(Λ(m)-1)(M(⌊(X-t)/m⌋)-M(D)) for successive square windows. Compute the signed TT* cross-energy 2⟨F,B⟩/(||F||²+||B||²) packet by packet. If the balanced packets fail to approach the cancellation sign, or the residual energy has exponent 2-o(1), the proposed spectral-gap mechanism is dead; success only licenses the analytic TT* calculation.
rung1_version: Prove the same signed dispersion estimate with right side X^{7/4+ε}. Stieltjes transfer and the prime-power term then give windowed mean square ≪X^{7/4+ε}, hence the canonical pointwise bound S≪X^{7/8+ε}, a genuine fixed power saving with δ=1/8.
plausible_partial: A Lean-formalizable square-window hyperbola lemma: throughout 0≤t<D, prove the stable-support identity for A_D(X-t), the exact μ*Λ=-μ log reduction, and a Stieltjes-transfer theorem showing that weighted ψ-dispersion plus a separately stated signed prime-power dispersion implies the Abel-face window bound. Analytically, one balanced dyadic packet bound with a power saving is a bounded-effort first theorem even before summing all packets.
weakest_assumption: A uniform signed Type-II dispersion estimate for the balanced dyadic packets of the paired log-Möbius/full-edge expression, strong enough to save X^η after summing O(log²X) packets; no pointwise Mertens bound, zero-free strip, or separate estimate for either half is assumed.
